issues.legal_issue: An appeal does not abate for failure to substitute the legal representatives of a deceased respondent when that respondent transferred the interest in dispute to parties already on record before death.
material_facts: Three respondents died after selling their respective shares by registered sale deeds to other respondents who were already parties to the appeal.
The transferred interests had devolved on those existing parties before the sellers died.
issues.conclusion: The appeal did not abate, and there was no need to bring the deceased respondents’ legal representatives on record or transpose them as legal representatives.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, when an interest in dispute devolves by transfer during the proceeding, the transferees may continue as parties; where the transferees are already on record, substitution of the transferors’ legal representatives is unnecessary.

predicates.appeal_pending: An appeal involving the disputed interests was pending.
predicates.respondents_transferred_disputed_interes: The respondents transferred their interests in dispute to other persons before they died.
predicates.transferees_already_on_record: The persons who received the transferred interests were already parties to the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal is pending, respondents transfer their disputed interests before death, and the transferees are already parties, the appeal does not abate.

issues.legal_issue: A will may be upheld when its execution is supported and the circumstances relied on as suspicious lack a factual foundation.
material_facts: A son propounded his mother’s registered will, which was executed about eight years before her death.
The will left the estate to the son, which the courts below treated as a suspicious circumstance because it deprived the daughters of inheritance.
The challengers did not plead the will’s invalidity, and the evidence did not establish the alleged pressure to execute it; cross-examination did not challenge the will’s correctness.
The subordinate appellate court considered the circumstances and upheld the will, while the High Court reversed without examining the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The suspicions identified by the trial court had no factual foundation; the subordinate appellate court’s finding upholding the will was restored, and the properties covered by it were excluded from partition.
issues.legal_principle: The propounder of a will must prove it and remove genuine suspicious features. Suspicion must be real, germane, and valid, not fanciful. The absence of a pleading challenging the will under Order 8 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the absence of evidence or cross-examination supporting the alleged pressure, were relevant to whether the asserted suspicion had a factual basis. No earlier case is identified by name in the judgment.

predicates.will_contested_in_partition_case: A party disputed a will that affected which property was available for partition.
predicates.will_execution_supported: Evidence was presented in support of the will’s execution.
predicates.will_made_years_before_testator_died: The testator lived for years after executing the will.
predicates.challengers_did_not_plead_or_testify_to_: The challengers neither pleaded nor gave evidence that pressure had been applied to obtain the will.

issues.definition: When a disputed will in a partition case is supported by evidence, the challengers do not support their allegations of coercion or other wrongdoing with facts, and the lower appellate court upholds it on the evidence, the will is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court’s reversal of a factual finding upholding a will is unsustainable when it does not examine the evidence supporting that finding.
material_facts: The subordinate appellate court considered the circumstances and evidence and upheld the will.
The High Court reversed that finding in a brief statement agreeing with the trial court, without examining the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment was set aside and the subordinate appellate court’s finding was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A court reviewing a factual finding must examine the evidence before upsetting it; merely reciting or adopting a conclusion without reviewing the evidence does not provide a basis to reverse a finding reached after consideration of the circumstances. The judgment cites no earlier case by name for this proposition.

predicates.second_appeal: The challenged decision was made in a second appeal.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_upheld_will_after_: The lower appellate court considered the evidence and upheld the will.
predicates.high_court_reversed_without_examining_ev: The High Court reversed that finding without examining the evidence.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, when the lower appellate court has upheld a will after considering the evidence, a High Court reversal without examining that evidence is unsustainable.
